hints.title: Parity Invariance
hints.text: Notice that adding or subtracting two preserves the parity of each integer. Odd elements can only transform into odd elements and even into even.

hints.title: Independent Matching
hints.text: Divide both arrays into separate sorted collections of even and odd values. Pair elements in monotonic order.

hints.title: Operation Aggregation
hints.text: Calculate absolute differences between corresponding sorted pairs. Each step changes one element by +2 and another by -2, so divide total positive differences by two (or total absolute differences by four).

hints.title: Optimal Pairing Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def makeSimilar(self, nums: list[int], target: list[int]) -> int:
        nums_even = sorted([x for x in nums if x % 2 == 0])
        nums_odd = sorted([x for x in nums if x % 2 != 0])
        tgt_even = sorted([x for x in target if x % 2 == 0])
        tgt_odd = sorted([x for x in target if x % 2 != 0])
        diff = sum(abs(a - b) for a, b in zip(nums_even, tgt_even)) + sum(abs(a - b) for a, b in zip(nums_odd, tgt_odd))
        return diff // 4
```

variables: n: length of nums and target
complexity.notes: Sorting separated parity partitions dominates the runtime.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Arbitrary element adjustment without sorting order requires quadratic search and risks suboptimal pair matches.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(n) auxiliary memory to partition odd and even elements.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Identifies parity invariance and sorts partitions to apply a greedy matching strategy.
